newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: "APEC lanes" bring chaos to Manila's streets.
newsitem.headline: "APEC lanes" bring chaos to Manila's streets.

text.p: A traffic scheme reserving special lanes for APEC delegates created massive jams in Manila streets on Tuesday but officials said Filipinos should bear the temporary inconvenience to give the country a good image.

Under the scheme, two of four lanes in several major streets were reserved exclusively for the use of the APEC visitors from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. from Tuesday until Monday's summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

The scheme, which intends to allow delegates easy access to their hotels, meeting venues and shopping malls, requires ordinary motorists to use the remaining lanes only. But the lanes assigned to ordinary motorists proved too narrow, creating what presidential press secretary Hector Villanueva called "horrible traffic".

Traffic jams were so bad in some streets that irate motorists spilled onto the so-called APEC Friendship Lanes and raced to their destinations. "Filipinos should have a little patience ... We can't make our guests fly," police general Romeo Maganto, who is in charge of implementing the scheme, told Reuters. "If our guests get stuck in traffic jams, we would create a bad impression around the world. They would think we are worse than Bangkok," he said referring to the Thai capital's notorious traffic jams.
Traffic in Manila, with more than one million vehicles on the roads daily, is bad even on normal days.

Police reported traffic jams stretching as far as seven km (four miles) on Roxas Boulevard which runs past the convention centre where ministerial meetings will be held ahead of the summit. The summit itself will be held at Subic Bay free port, northwest of Manila.
Alan Tolosa, deputy chief of the leftist New Patriotic Alliance (Bayan) denounced the "Friendship Lanes" as a discrimination against Filipinos.

"Why should we have Friendship Lanes for APEC. These 18 APEC leaders are not friendly to us. They will be exploiting our economies and stealing our resources," Tolosa said, referring to APEC's goal of liberalising trade and investment.
